proof.text: Let T be the identity etale X-scheme. The given family defines arrows V_i -> T. Its generated sieve R is covering by Mathlib Scheme.ofArrows_mem_smallEtaleTopology_iff and hcover [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. For every test object U, pull R back along U -> T; GrothendieckTopology.pullback_stable makes this a covering sieve of U. This uses the existing topology directly, without choosing fibre products.

proof.text: For an arrow W -> U in the pulled-back sieve, membership in the generated sieve gives an index i and an X-morphism b : W -> V_i. Thus Over.mk b is an object of the slice at V_i. Evaluate the identity-equals-zero equation supplied by IsZero (F.over V_i) at this object. Slice restriction is presheaf composition, so this is precisely id_{F(W)} = 0 and proves IsZero F(W). The empty-family case has no such arrows and requires no choice.

proof.text: Apply Presheaf.IsSheaf.hom_ext to the identity and zero endomorphisms of F(U), using the pulled-back covering sieve. Each restricted pair has zero target F(W) by the previous step, so the pair is equal. Hence id_{F(U)} = 0 for every U. Natural transformation extensionality and Sheaf.hom_ext give id_F = 0, which implies IsZero F by IsZero.iff_id_eq_zero. All uses are generic categorical sheaf facts, valid for ModuleCat coefficients.

title: An etale module sheaf vanishing on a covering family is zero
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $\{\varphi_i:V_i\to X\}_{i\in I}$ be a covering family of $X$ in its small etale site $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], that is, a finite or arbitrary jointly surjective family of etale morphisms; for example a finite family of open immersions [def-weil-open-immersion] whose images cover $X$, and, when $X$ is empty, the empty family. Let $F$ be a sheaf of modules on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], and write $F|_{V_i}$ for its restriction to the slice site $X_{\mathrm{et}}/V_i$, whose sections over an etale $X$-morphism $W\to V_i$ are $F(W)$. If every restriction $F|_{V_i}$ is the zero sheaf, then $F$ is the zero sheaf on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$.
